text:
Maya: FYI I've been seeing a spike in prefetch+soft-evict thrash on a few busy tenants — prefetched prefixes immediately get demoted and then re-requested. Thinking about a "leaseback" idea: when we soft-evict a prefix, give it a tiny reclaimable lease so hot clients can re-attach without the full prefetch cost. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

Vikram: Can you clarify the semantics? Is leaseback just a short-lived soft-pin? How do we avoid serving stale data or violating write-after-read guarantees?

Maya: Not a full pin. Idea is: on demote we attach a short reclaim token and keep the KV metadata (no slab pin). Reclaiming checks token+epoch; if a write happened that invalidates epoch, reclaim fails and client triggers normal prefetch. So correctness delegates to epoch/version check, not cache TTL.

Sam: Two quick concerns: 1) handshake/race with handoff tokens — if two nodes think they can reclaim, who wins? 2) read vs write paths — we must avoid allowing leaseback to serve writes unless we have a write lease.

Aisha: Agree with Sam. Suggest mode separation: `read-only` leaseback vs `promote-to-pin` flow that requires an atomic acquire with the ownership service. Heuristics for window: prefer short (500ms-5s) and bounded reclaims per-tenant. Example config sketch:```leaseback { window_ms: 2000 max_reclaims: 3 mode: "read-only" }```

Vikram: Also add a per-shard reclaim budget counter to prevent blowups during storms. Metric ideas: `kv.leaseback.reclaims`, `kv.leaseback.failures`, `kv.leaseback.reclaim_latency_ms` so ops can tune.

Maya: Good call. On correctness: reclaim succeeds only if cached metadata epoch == latest known epoch for that prefix. If mismatch, we must fall back to prefetch and surface a `reclaim_stale` metric.

Sam: For races between two reclaimers: the reclaim operation should be a CAS on the token field in the prefix descriptor. If CAS fails, the loser should either trigger async prefetch or return `try_prefetch`. That keeps API simple.

Aisha: We should also consider workload-aware thresholds: don't allow leaseback for tenants marked `strict_consistency=true` or for prefixes with heavy write rates. Maybe expose knobs at tenant level.

Maya: Proposed rollout plan: implement as `read-only` reclaim first, unit tests for CAS/race, synthetic chaos test that kills nodes mid-reclaim, then a 1% canary on dedicated pools, observe `reclaims/failures` and tail latencies for reads. If stable, enable `promote-to-pin` path behind feature flag.

Sam: Fallback behavior detail: if reclaim fails and prefetch would block, prefer returning a short-circuit error (`E_RECLAIM_NEEDED`) so callers can decide (sync prefetch vs degrade). We should avoid blocking critical read qps.

Maya: Action items: @Vikram prototype token CAS & metrics, @Sam add API error code and client guidance, @Aisha add heuristics + tenant config, I'll draft RFC with invariants and test plan. I'll open a PR for a minimal `read-only` reclaim within 24h.

evict-bot: Note: created ticket INF-2341 with title "leaseback reclaim prototype" and assigned to Maya, Vikram, Sam, Aisha. Scheduled canary label: `canary/1pct`. :white_check_mark:

Maya: Thanks — I'll post the RFC link here once it's up and include a small simulation script to validate reclaim budget. :rocket:
